title: Energy and Transformations
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Energy and Transformations Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Energy can be transformed: forms of energy (kinetic, light, sound, thermal, elastic, chemical, electrical, gravitational), conservation of energy, and devices that change one form of energy into another. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 4, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets (BC): forms of energy, energy changes in devices, renewable and non-renewable resources, and saving energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy changes form but is never used up.
key_sub: A flashlight changes chemical energy into light.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy comes in many forms: kinetic (motion), light, sound, thermal (heat), elastic (stretched or squashed), chemical (stored in food and fuel), electrical and gravitational. Energy is conserved: it is not made or destroyed, only changed from one form to another.

Devices transform energy: a flashlight turns the chemical energy in batteries into light (and some heat); a wind-up toy turns elastic energy into kinetic energy.

Example

A battery-powered fan: what energy change happens?

Battery → electricity → motion

Answer: chemical to electrical to kinetic

Example

What energy does a stretched elastic band store?

It springs back.

Answer: elastic energy

Common mistakes

  • Saying energy gets used up (it changes form).
  • Forgetting the heat that every device gives off.
  • Mixing up energy forms and energy sources.

faq.a: Energy from sources that are replaced naturally, like sunlight, wind and flowing water.

faq.q: Where does the energy in food come from?
faq.a: From the Sun, stored by plants as chemical energy.

items.q: Which form of energy does a running dog mainly have?
items.e: It is moving.

items.q: What is the main source of energy for the Earth?
items.e: Plants, animals, food and fuels all depend on the Sun.

items.q: Where did the energy in the rice we eat first come from?
items.e: The rice plant used light energy from the Sun to make food.

items.q: An object is lifted higher. What happens to its gravitational potential energy?
items.e: The higher it is, the more gravitational potential energy it has.

items.q: Which form of energy does the warmth from a gas stove mainly have?
items.e: This is heat energy.

items.q: Where did the energy in a chicken drumstick first come from?
items.e: The chicken ate plants, which got their energy from the Sun.

items.q: Which form of energy does a compressed spring in a toy mainly have?
items.e: It is stretched, bent or compressed.

items.q: A stretched elastic band stores which form of energy?
items.e: It is released when let go.

items.q: Which form of energy does a piece of charcoal for a barbecue mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of burning fossil fuels?
c: It releases carbon dioxide and pollutes the air.
items.e: Fossil fuels add greenhouse gases.

items.q: Which form of energy does a moving object have?
items.e: The faster it moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

items.q: Can energy be created or destroyed?
c: No. It can only be converted from one form to another.
items.e: The total amount of energy stays the same.

items.q: Which form of energy does a ball rolling down a slope mainly have?
items.e: It is moving.

items.q: Where did the energy in gasoline first come from?
items.e: Gasoline comes from living things of long ago, which got their energy from the Sun.

items.q: Which form of energy is stored in food?
items.e: Your body changes it into motion and heat.

items.q: Which form of energy does the bent bow of an archer, ready to shoot mainly have?
items.e: It is stretched, bent or compressed.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of wind turbines?
c: They only work when the wind blows.
items.e: Every source has pros and cons.

items.q: Why should you put on a sweater instead of turning up the heat?
c: It makes the house warmer for everyone.
items.e: Conserving energy reduces pollution.

items.q: Why are LED bulbs better than old incandescent bulbs?
c: They give the same light using much less electricity.
They are brighter only because they are hot.
items.e: Less energy is wasted as heat.

items.q: What does the Energy Star label on an appliance mean?
c: It runs on solar power only.
It uses less energy than similar models.
items.e: Look for efficient appliances.

items.q: An electric fan changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of an electric fan is to make motion.

items.q: A pupil cycles up a slope and stops at the top. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → chemical potential energy
chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy
items.e: A pupil cycles up a slope and stops at the top: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy.

items.q: A toy car with a motor changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a toy car with a motor is to make motion.

items.q: A microphone changes sound into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a microphone is to make electric energy.

items.q: An electric stove changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of an electric stove is to make heat.

items.q: Which device changes light into electric energy?
c: a bike light powered by the wheel
items.e: Look at what goes in (light) and what comes out (electric energy).

items.q: A phone's ringer changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a phone's ringer is to make sound.

items.q: A pupil eats breakfast and then runs to school. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy
items.e: A pupil eats breakfast and then runs to school: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: A plant makes food in its leaves. Which shows the main energy conversion?
items.e: A plant makes food in its leaves: light energy → chemical potential energy.

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into motion?
c: a toy car with a motor
a bike light powered by the wheel
items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (motion).

items.q: An electric drill changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of an electric drill is to make motion.

items.q: A candle burns. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy
light energy and heat energy → chemical potential energy
items.e: A candle burns: chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy.

items.q: A battery powers a flashlight. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy
chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy
light energy → electrical energy → chemical potential energy
items.e: A battery powers a flashlight: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy.

items.q: Which is the main energy change in a battery-powered flashlight?
items.e: The battery stores chemical energy.

items.q: A lamp changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a lamp is to make light.

items.q: A hair dryer changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a hair dryer is to make heat.

items.q: A hand-crank flashlight changes motion (energy of motion) into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a hand-crank flashlight is to make light.

items.q: A wind turbine changes motion (energy of motion) into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a wind turbine is to make electric energy.

items.q: Which device changes light into electric energy?
items.e: Look at what goes in (light) and what comes out (electric energy).

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into heat?
c: a bike light powered by the wheel
items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (heat).

items.q: Which is used to turn heat inside Earth into electricity or motion?
c: a dam with a power plant
items.e: Energy from heat inside Earth is used with a geothermal power plant.

items.q: Owen asks how copper and gold ores formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
items.e: Copper and gold ores formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries.

items.q: People use a coal power plant to get energy from coal. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It is replaced naturally in a few days.
It can make electricity day and night.
items.e: It can make electricity day and night.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Heat from inside Earth (geothermal) is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: People use wind turbines to get energy from wind. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.
Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.
Burning gas pollutes the air, and drilling can harm land and water.
A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.
items.e: Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.

items.q: Ava asks how coal formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
items.e: Coal formed from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years.

items.q: Noah reads about a resource that formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how oil and natural gas formed.

items.q: Aiden asks how rock salt formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
items.e: Rock salt formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago.

items.q: Ava asks how oil and natural gas formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
items.e: Oil and natural gas formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years.

items.q: Ava asks how groundwater formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
items.e: Groundwater formed from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers).

items.q: Sofia reads about a resource that formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how copper and gold ores formed.

items.q: People use a gas stove or gas power plant to get energy from natural gas. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Burning gas pollutes the air, and drilling can harm land and water.
It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.
Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.
items.e: Burning gas pollutes the air, and drilling can harm land and water.

items.q: Benjamin asks how iron ore formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
items.e: Iron ore formed from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Wind is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: People use gasoline in cars to get energy from oil. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.
Burning gasoline pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.
items.e: Burning gasoline pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.

items.q: People use a geothermal power plant to get energy from heat inside Earth. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.
Burning gasoline pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.
It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
items.e: It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Flowing water is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: Why is energy never really 'used up'?
c: It changes from one form to another.
items.e: Energy is conserved.

items.q: Which action saves energy at home?
c: leaving the TV on all night
opening windows with the heat on
turning off lights when you leave a room
items.e: Small actions add up.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Oil formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: Which of the three R's is putting aluminum cans in the recycling bin?
items.e: Recycling means breaking a material down to make new products.

items.q: An old bulb uses 75 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 11 watts. A school replaces 4 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (75 − 11) × 4 = 256 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: A town's wells are running low in summer. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.
Fix leaks and water lawns less often.
Use reusable cloth bags and ban single-use plastic bags.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Fix leaks and water lawns less often.

items.q: What energy change happens when you rub your hands together?
items.e: Friction makes heat.

items.q: Which of the three R's is taking glass bottles to be made into new glass?
items.e: Recycling means breaking a material down to make new products.

items.q: A town burns coal to make electricity, polluting the air. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Build wind turbines and solar panels.
Fix leaks and water lawns less often.
Build a treatment plant that cleans wastewater before it is released.
Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertilizer.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Build wind turbines and solar panels.

items.q: Deer are hit by cars where a highway cuts through their habitat. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Build a wildlife bridge over the highway.
Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.
Add garbage and recycling bins and hold clean-up days.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Build a wildlife bridge over the highway.

items.q: Which of the three R's is turning off lights in empty rooms?
items.e: Reducing means using less in the first place.

items.q: Which of the three R's is buying fewer items with plastic packaging?
items.e: Reducing means using less in the first place.

items.q: Soil washes off a farm field into a river after heavy rain. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.
Start a recycling and composting program.
Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertilizer.
Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.

items.q: Which of the three R's is donating outgrown clothes?
items.e: Reusing means using something again for the same or a new job.

items.q: An old bulb uses 40 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 6 watts. A school replaces 8 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (40 − 6) × 8 = 272 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: What does 'reduce, reuse, recycle' help save?
c: resources and the energy needed to make new things
items.e: Making new products uses energy.

items.q: Which of the three R's is sending old newspapers to make new paper?
items.e: Recycling means breaking a material down to make new products.

items.q: An old bulb uses 60 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 10 watts. A school replaces 4 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (60 − 10) × 4 = 200 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: Which of the three R's is using a refillable water bottle?
items.e: Reusing means using something again for the same or a new job.

items.q: Which of the three R's is recycling plastic bottles into fleece jackets?
items.e: Recycling means breaking a material down to make new products.

items.q: An old bulb uses 60 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 9 watts. A school replaces 5 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (60 − 9) × 5 = 255 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: Which is a non-renewable energy source?
items.e: Fossil fuels took millions of years to form.

items.q: Which of the three R's is walking to school instead of being driven?
items.e: Reducing means using less in the first place.

items.q: A shower uses about 8 litres of water per minute. Noah cuts his shower from 10 minutes to 8 minutes. How much water does that save in 7 days?
Why do some cities build wetlands next to farms?
c: Wetland plants trap soil and fertilizer before they reach rivers.
items.e: Wetlands act like natural filters.

items.q: A shower uses about 9 litres of water per minute. Ethan cuts his shower from 12 minutes to 4 minutes. How much water does that save in 7 days?
Which statement about individual actions is most accurate?
c: Small actions by many people can add up to a big difference.
items.e: If thousands of families save water, the total saved is huge.

items.q: What percent of Lakeview's electricity comes from fossil fuels?
items.e: Coal (10%) + natural gas (30%) = 40%.

items.q: Why do engineers test a design more than once?
c: to see if the results are the same and the design is reliable
items.e: Repeated tests show if the design really works.

items.q: A town wants to know if its new recycling program works. What should it measure?
c: how many people like the program
the amount of garbage sent to the landfill before and after
items.e: Data before and after the change show whether less waste goes to the landfill.

items.q: Mei's rubber-band car rolls 2 metres. How could she make it go farther?
c: wind the rubber band more times
items.e: More winding stores more energy that changes into motion.

items.q: A community bans cutting trees near a river. What is the most likely result?
c: Less erosion and cleaner, cooler water for fish.
Fewer fish because there is shade.
items.e: Tree roots hold the banks and shade keeps the water cool.

items.q: What percent of Riverton's electricity comes from renewable sources?
items.e: Wind and solar (35%) + water (5%) = 40%.

items.q: A school installs solar panels. Which problem does this help with?
c: It reduces the electricity made by burning fossil fuels.
items.e: Solar panels make electricity without burning fuel.
